title: The graph: why SRS needs a graph element

sections.name: claim
sections.label: Claim
sections.content: SRS needs a graph element (owner, 2026-10-30, vignette in conversation 2026-10-29). In the owner's earlier words the need is for relationships and links: "seeing relationships ... systems in systems" (lenses assessment, 2026-10-09). No vignette uses the word graph.

sections.name: story
sections.label: The story so far
sections.content:
SRS was always a graph: records joined by typed, binary relations. In September we ruled that meaning lives in relations and membership is declared (srs decision 0750c62f). What was missing was evidence for a graph surface, so every relation feature nobody used was removed with a return trigger: relation-query in 0 of 13 real sections, relation provenance in 0 of 250 relations (srs decision 4f1e12e5).

Those triggers are now firing:
- A third-party demo had to restate 296 evidences edges as container membership to print one problem dossier (finding bbe2be46, srs#726).
- Clients and agents rebuild the same walks (reach, lineage, neighbours) in their own code, and the one picture, the Map, breaks past a few hundred records (finding on the graph surface, this thread).
- People cannot see what links to what (SP-48, vignettes 2941f51a and 35e35dd2).
- Federation's return, the graph across repositories, is ratified (decision 31e9fd27).

The need the evidence supports is narrow: one-hop selection by relation, visible links (what links here), and a bounded walk in the core. It is not a graph query language (strategy contract 0ce48b8d), and keeping that line is what separates it from the unplanned query surface removed in srs#525.

sections.name: strands
sections.label: Strands and evidence
sections.content:
1. See the graph: SP-48 (7063a8d7), remedy lenses (364126da), vignettes 2941f51a and 35e35dd2, srs-web#481 (Map at 704 records), muDemocracy-decisions#21 (2026-03-17, earliest request found).
2. Select by relation: finding bbe2be46, vignette d6fd498b, srs#726 open question 3 and the owner's 'planned query language' (srs#688), srs#851 (33 container literals), SP-24 (bc432d78).
3. Removed, awaiting evidence: srs decision 4f1e12e5 (item 4 relation-query, item 2 federation), strategy contract e1cd52e7.
4. Integrity already done: RFC-005 installable relation types, RFC-027 relation rows, RFC-022 relational lifecycle states, srs#171 and srs#287 (relation layer), srs decision 0750c62f; missing constraints: unit cf9f5816 (acyclicity, cardinality), srs-context finding e1d026a5 (the concept graph is not a DAG).
5. Agents navigating by relation: srs-rust#1413, #1415, #1416, #1229; srs-context finding 030997a9 and SP-22 (d199abac) on context cost; finding bbe9faf9 (zero-context agent).
6. Across repositories: decision 31e9fd27, SP-86 (c8167ce7), SP-87 (11cd5900), cluster c583f5d7, strategy contract 586cd1ec, SP-09 (7a0a13f1).

sections.name: counter
sections.label: Counter-evidence
sections.content:
- Strategy contract 0ce48b8d: the discovery contract excludes a general graph query language; srs#726: a query must never become a place meaning lives.
- A record of dead relation features (4f1e12e5): relation-query 0 of 13, provenance 0 of 250, the old federation 34 prose records with no data.
- Carried context 287d4071: lifecycle needs looked like graph walking but were met twice without graph code.
- Finding bbe2be46: one hop was enough; nothing needed multi-hop.
- Decision 559bfb9e (experiment now, unify later) and one-way-per-goal: a derived container would be a third selection construct, and 0750c62f says no third.
- srs docs/research/graph-model-alignment.md (2026-08-10, srs#368 open): SRS does not need to adopt a graph model.
- srs-rust#1086: unwanted contains expansion in rendering.

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open questions
sections.content:
- Does selection need more than one hop? Only one corpus (LiveWyer) has been measured.
- Where does a graph view sit: a lens layout, a Composition, or a new presentation object?
- Is a walk (srs-rust#1413) a core service or a DiscoveryQuery axis? One way per goal says not both.
- Is any cross-repository graph needed before RFC-049 is accepted?
- Must integrity constraints (acyclicity, cardinality) come first?
- Has anyone outside the owner's projects asked for a graph view?
- No affirmed problem names relation selection itself (srs-rust#1413 says so); SP-24 and SP-48 carry it today.
